schedule: before 07:00 on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Non-major updates merge themselves. The inherited preset already holds them for 3 days (minimumReleaseAge) and CI covers every shipped TFM plus package API validation, so a human gate adds delay without adding signal.
Majors always get a human. They are where breaking changes and semver decisions live.
Dependencies that ship inside a package become a patch release: consumers get a raised dependency floor.
Test, sample and CI dependencies never reach a consumer, so they merge without cutting a release. `chore` is the type release-please ignores.

Central Package Management puts every version in one file, which defeats path-based routing. Versions there are overwhelmingly test/sample dependencies; the one shipped dependency (OpenTelemetry) is routed to `fix` by the rule below. Release explicitly when in doubt — see MAINTAINERS.md.

Dependencies that ship inside a package: OpenTelemetry (Altinn.AspNet.HealthChecks.OpenTelemetry) and AspNetCore.HealthChecks.Uris (Altinn.AspNet.HealthChecks.Probes). Their updates warrant a release. Ungrouped (groupName: null) so they never ride along in the shared non-major PR — that keeps `does this commit cut a release?` a property of a single PR rather than of whatever happened to be batched with it. Add any new src/** PackageReference here.

Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost is versioned in lockstep with the shared framework. The test project has one line per TFM; each must stay inside its own major band or the net8.0/net9.0 legs stop building.
The SDK in global.json gates what CI and every contributor builds with. Worth a look even for a patch bump.
